title: Private deployments backup & restore playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This draft playbook captures disaster recovery (DR) and backup/restore procedures for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem bundles). It combines operational runbooks, Terraform module notes, and upgrade checklist items that must be executed before, during, and after upgrades or DR events. The doc is intentionally prescriptive to reduce ambiguity during incidents; follow runbook steps and escalate per the on-call rota.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployment customers running Redwood control plane + inference nodes (K8s or bare-metal), Postgres metadata DB, object storage for model/artifact blobs, and any local KV caches.
- Assumes remote Terraform state is stored in an S3-compatible bucket with state locking (DynamoDB lock used for AWS; consul/etcd for on-prem).
- Assumes backups encrypted with CMK (KMS) and keys available to the on-call/team; if KMS unavailable, follow key-recovery SOP linked in artifacts.
- RPO/RTO targets should be specified per-customer in the deployment contract; default targets: RPO = 1 hour, RTO = 4 hours for metadata DB and control-plane reconnection; model artifact restore is best-effort depending on object storage size.

DR objectives (default):
- RPO: 1 hour (DB WAL + hourly backups)
- RTO: 4 hours (restore DB + control plane)
- Validation: self-checking smoke tests and end-to-end inference test within 30 minutes post-restore

Backup inventory and cadence:
- Postgres (metadata DB): Continuous WAL shipping + nightly base backup (pg_basebackup) stored to S3-compatible bucket. Retention: 30 days by default, configurable in terraform var backup_retention_days.
- Object storage (models, artifacts): Versioned object store (MinIO or S3). Daily snapshot + on-write immutability option for compliant customers. Retention: 90 days.
- Kubernetes cluster state: Velero backups of namespaces containing Redwood services (control plane, operators). Frequency: every 4 hours for control-plane namespaces. Retention: 14 days.
- Configuration and secrets: Terraform state + encrypted secrets (SOPS) stored in repo; configuration snapshots exported nightly to artifacts bucket.
- KV caches (if persisted): periodic snapshots according to TTL, persisted to object store every hour.

Storage targets and encryption:
- Primary: customer-provided S3-compatible endpoint (MinIO/Wasabi/Cloud). Buckets: redwood-<deployment>-backups-<env>.
- Encryption: server-side (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) or client-side with CMK. Use KMS keys with alias redwood/private-<customer>-cmk when possible.

Terraform module notes (important for DR correctness):
- modules/backups:
  - Variables: backup_bucket, retention_days, wal_shipper_enabled, kms_key_arn, velero_schedule_cron.
  - Lifecycle: terraform resource aws_s3_bucket has lifecycle prevent_destroy = true for backup buckets by default; to delete you must set allow_backup_bucket_destroy = true in vars and follow approval workflow.
  - State: remote state must use locking. When performing restores that update terraform-managed resources (e.g., replacing control-plane nodes), ensure terraform state lock is obtained and a plan is reviewed.
- modules/terraform-state: include dynamodb_table for locking (AWS) or consul backend config for on-prem. Mistakes here lead to concurrent changes and inconsistent restores.
- Upgrade-related flags: expose a boolean variable dr_snapshot_before_upgrade. Upgrade pipelines (CI) must set this flag to true for major/minor upgrades to trigger a full snapshot.
- Recommended provider pinning: provider versions must be fixed in modules to reduce plan drift during emergency restores.

Upgrade plan notes (pre-upgrade DR steps):
1) Preflight: run pre-upgrade checks (disk space, node readiness, TLS cert validity, kube versions).
2) Create full backups: trigger pg_basebackup + Velero backup + object-store snapshot. Tag backups with upgrade_<semver>_<timestamp>.
3) Lock terraform state and record current plan output.
4) If upgrade involves DB migration, run migrations in canary cluster first (see canary-test checklist).
5) Record and export current metrics dashboards and alert policies.
6) Notify customer and CS with expected maintenance window and rollback plan.

Primary recovery runbook (full control plane + DB loss):
A. Initial triage (first 15 minutes)
  - Confirm scope: entire region/datacenter vs single-cluster.
  - Pager duty: notify eng-private-deployments on-call.
  - Gather artifacts: latest backup timestamps, S3 bucket health, Terraform state bucket access, KMS key access.

B. Restore metadata DB (target RTO critical path)
  - If base backup exists and WAL segments available: restore using pg_basebackup + point-in-time recovery. Example (object-store):
    - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-<deploy>/pgbase/2026-03-09-base.tar.gz /var/lib/pgsql/
    - tar -xzf 2026-03-09-base.tar.gz -C /var/lib/pgsql/
    - configure recovery.conf with restore_command='aws s3 cp s3://redwood-<deploy>/pg_wal/%f %p' and recovery_target_time='2026-03-09T10:43:00Z'
    - systemctl start postgresql
  - If WAL missing, restore to most recent base backup and accept data loss to last successful WAL. Document RPO impact.
  - Post-restore: run schema checks: psql -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM migrations WHERE applied = false;'

C. Restore object storage (models/artifacts)
  - For smaller models: rclone copy s3://redwood-<deploy>/models/ s3://redwood-restore/
  - For large buckets: consider partial or on-demand restore and update the filesystem pointer in model-service to point to the restored bucket prefix.

D. Restore Kubernetes control plane and operators
  - Restore Velero backup: velero restore create --from-backup <backup-name> --namespace redwood-control-plane
  - Wait for CRDs and operators to become Ready.
  - Reconcile Helm releases: helm upgrade --install redwood-control-plane ./charts/control-plane -f restored-values.yaml

E. Reconfigure networking and DNS
  - If public endpoints moved, update DNS records (internal DNS or Route53).
  - Validate VPC peering, security groups, and NACLs.

F. Smoke tests and validation (target within 30 minutes of control plane up)
  - API health endpoint check: curl -sS https://<endpoint>/healthz | grep ok
  - End-to-end inference test with small model: run e2e test harness and verify latency < SLOs and responses are within expected quality.
  - Cost/usage sanity: check that billing tokens/usage counters are consistent.

G. Post-restore: incident report and timeline
  - Capture commands run, artifacts used, restore point, RTO/RPO achieved, and follow-up items (bug fixes, test gaps).
  - Schedule DR retro and update playbook accordingly.

Scenario-specific notes and tips:
- Corrupted data detected: if corruption limited to a table, use logical dump (pg_dump) from last good backup and restore specific tables rather than full cluster recovery to reduce RTO.
- Control-plane node rebuilds: prefer replacing nodes via terraform apply after state lock; avoid manual changes that diverge from terraform unless explicitly approved.
- Terraform state restore: if state file corrupted, use state backup copies under s3://redwood-state-backups/<deployment>/ and run terraform state replace-provider / state rm as needed. Keep an immutable copy of the state for last 7 days.

Commands and quick references (examples):
- Trigger a manual DB base backup from primary: pg_basebackup -h localhost -D /backups/base -U backup_user -Fp -Xs -P
- WAL shipping via wal-g: wal-g backup-push /var/lib/pgsql/data
- Velero schedule list: velero schedule get -n redwood-control-plane
- Velero restore: velero restore create --from-backup backup-2026-03-09-04 --wait
- Terraform state list/lock: terraform init && terraform plan -lock=true -input=false

Testing and drills:
- Quarterly DR drill: full restore to isolated environment (not staging) with production-sized data (sampled if cost-sensitive). Execute full runbook end-to-end and record RTO/RPO.
- Monthly partial test: restore metadata DB to staging and run smoke tests.
- After each major terraform module change: run restore simulation where state is exported and a dry-run apply is tested against an isolated copy.

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- After every drill or real incident, document gaps and assign remediation work items (infra bugs, missing monitoring, terraform module improvements).
- Keep a changelog inside the backups module describing format changes and compatibility (e.g., WAL naming changes, velero version compatibility).

Open action items (work-in-progress):
- [ ] Add terraform variable to toggle pre-upgrade ephemeral snapshot for object storage (assigned: Miguel).
- [ ] Harden S3 bucket policies to limit deletions during retention window (assigned: Dana).
- [ ] Add automated smoke test harness that runs after Velero restores (assigned: Priya).

Contacts and escalation:
- eng-private-deployments on-call: pager (pagerduty link internal)
- Backup module owner: Miguel Herrera 
- Terraform state owner: Platform Eng (Slack: #platform-terraform)

References and further reading:
- velero restore docs: https://velero.io/docs/
- pg_basebackup and PITR: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/backup.html
- Terraform remote state best practices: https://www.terraform.io/docs/state/overview.html

Notes/footnotes:
- This document is a draft. Confirm environment-specific details (bucket names, KMS ARNs, backup schedules) from the deployment manifest before executing any destructive steps.
- Where possible prefer automation (backup triggers, terraform pipelines) over manual procedures to reduce human error.

Revision history: 2025-11-05 initial draft by Aisha; 2026-01-20 added terraform module notes (Miguel); 2026-03-10 updated RTO/RPO defaults and pre-upgrade checklist (Priya).
